## gaming_hud_mockup

> Fictional video-game HUD mockup with health and mana bars, minimap, mission objective overlay.

**Artifact:** `mockup`, `1920x1088`, aspect `16:9`
**Demo vars:** `templates/gaming/_vars_examples/gaming_hud_mockup.yml`

### English

```
[1. Subject] A 16:9 in-game heads-up-display mockup for the fictional title Embergate Saga. The image must read as a single in-game frame captured mid-play — a stylized environment view with the HUD layered on top: a corner health and mana cluster, a circular minimap, a slim mission-objective banner, and a top-bar with the game-title overlay.
[2. Action] The HUD must feel functional, not decorative. The health and mana indicators show the value 62% on the health bar, the minimap shows a stylized region pin for Sunken Marsh of Velhar, and the objective banner names the current mission. The background environment looks paused mid-play — no characters mid-action, no fight effects.
[3. Scene] A muted painterly fantasy or sci-fi environment evoking the fictional location Sunken Marsh of Velhar. Foreground composition is deliberately quiet so the HUD can sit on top without competing. Lighting is even and atmospheric. No real-world buildings, no real-world IP references, no recognizable game-franchise assets.
[4. Composition] 16:9 frame. The HUD lives in three reserved zones: bottom-left holds a vertical stack of two value bars (red health on top, blue mana below) plus a small portrait silhouette; upper-right holds a circular minimap with cardinal markers; upper-center holds a slim banner with the mission objective; the very top edge holds a thin title overlay strip. The remaining ~70% of canvas is environment.
[5. Style] Stylized painterly game-art aesthetic with crisp UI on top. Environment uses muted RPG palette (slate, moss, dust) with a single signature accent. UI panels use a glass-and-metal frame style — semi-translucent dark fills, hairline metallic borders, legible game-display sans-serif. No platform watermark, no real HUD elements from existing games.

Text to render exactly (chunked into named slots):
- title_overlay: "Embergate Saga"
- location_label: "Sunken Marsh of Velhar"
- mission_objective: "Objective: find the witch's lantern"

Preserve (edit mode only):
- HUD spatial zones (corner clusters, top banner)
- bar fill levels matching hp_pct

NO: watermarks, signatures, real famous game franchise logos or assets, real platform HUD chrome (Xbox, PlayStation, Steam UI), real-celebrity likeness, clip-art icons, rainbow neon palette, lens flare overload, photographic real-world locations, generic stock UI kits
```

## gaming_item_card

> Vertical 3:4 collectible RPG/CCG-style item card with name, rarity ribbon, stat lines, and lore blurb.

**Artifact:** `poster`, `1152x1536`, aspect `3:4`
**Demo vars:** `templates/gaming/_vars_examples/gaming_item_card.yml`

### English

```
[1. Subject] A vertical 3:4 collectible item card in fantasy RPG / trading-card style for the item Sunfire Lantern. The card is the entire image — a single rectangular card face with rounded corners, framed border, hero illustration window, name banner, rarity ribbon, stat lines, and a lore blurb at the bottom. Nothing exists outside the card face itself.
[2. Action] Read the card top to bottom: the name reads first, the illustration anchors identity, the rarity ribbon signals worth, the stat block delivers mechanics, and the lore blurb closes the impression. There is no in-world action; the illustration shows the item at rest with diegetic light catching its key features.
[3. Scene] Inside the illustration window: a small, centered, slightly-3D item portrait set against a soft diorama background tied to the item's flavor. Around the illustration: an ornamented metallic card border with corner motifs. No physical environment outside the card face — the background of the rendered image is the card-bleed area, a flat dark field.
[4. Composition] 3:4 vertical card. Top ~9% holds a name banner across the width. Below it (~46% of the height) is the rectangular illustration window with rounded corners. A diagonal rarity ribbon sits in the upper-right corner of the illustration window. Below the illustration, two side-by-side stat lines sit in their own bordered tiles. The bottom ~16% holds a small lore-blurb panel with italic flavor text. Margins inside the card are generous.
[5. Style] Painterly fantasy card aesthetic — rich saturated illustration in the window, ornate but disciplined metallic frame around it, crisp display serif for the item name, small condensed sans-serif for stats and lore. Rarity color (e.g. gold for legendary, violet for epic) keys the ribbon and the frame highlights. No real-world branding, no franchise references.

Text to render exactly (chunked into named slots):
- item_name: "Sunfire Lantern"
- rarity: "Legendary"
- stat1: "+18 Light radius"
- stat2: "+6 Resolve"

Preserve (edit mode only):
- card frame structural border
- rarity color cue

NO: watermarks, signatures, real famous game franchise logos or assets, real-celebrity likeness, rainbow neon palette, clip-art icons, cluttered floating ornaments, chibi super-deformed proportions, lens flare, photographic real-world objects
```

## gaming_map_panel

> 16:9 fantasy world-map / quest-map panel with three labeled regions and a parchment border.

**Artifact:** `diagram`, `1920x1088`, aspect `16:9`
**Demo vars:** `templates/gaming/_vars_examples/gaming_map_panel.yml`

### English

```
[1. Subject] A 16:9 fantasy quest map of the fictional world Realm of Veyrhold, rendered as an in-game codex panel. The image is the full map framed by a parchment border with rolled-corner motifs. The map interior shows a single contiguous region with three named sub- regions, connecting routes, and small iconographic markers for settlements, perils, and waypoints.
[2. Action] Reading the map: the world title sits in a top cartouche; the three sub-regions are labeled at their geographic centers; routes connect them as dotted ink trails. The viewer should be able to trace a journey between the three labeled regions without ambiguity. No characters, no live battles — this is a static in-codex reference page.
[3. Scene] The "scene" is the map itself: stylized topography with hills, forest stipple, river ink lines, and a coastline. No real-world geography, no recognizable map projections of Earth, no real place names. The surrounding parchment border is a distinct framing element with worn edges and one corner scroll motif.
[4. Composition] 16:9 frame. Outer 7% is parchment border. The map interior fills the central area with the world-name cartouche pinned to the top edge (~9% tall). The three sub-regions are spaced as a rough triangle across the map — region 1 upper-left, region 2 middle- right, region 3 lower-center — each with a small icon and a label set in italic display. A small compass rose sits in the lower-right corner, a scale bar in the lower-left.
[5. Style] Hand-drawn fantasy cartography aesthetic — sepia and slate ink on cream parchment, fine cross-hatching for hills and forests, painterly water tones, italic display type for labels. Subtle paper grain and edge wear. No modern UI elements, no real-world cartographic features (no Mercator grid, no GPS pins).

Text to render exactly (chunked into named slots):
- world_name: "Realm of Veyrhold"
- region1: "Ashenmoor Highlands"
- region2: "Glasswind Coast"
- region3: "Sunken Reach"

Preserve (edit mode only):
- parchment border integrity
- relative region positions (UL, MR, LC)

NO: watermarks, signatures, real-world geography or place names, real famous game franchise logos or assets, modern UI elements, GPS pins or app-style icons, rainbow neon palette, clip-art icons, lens flare, photographic real terrain
```
